name: amici
title: Showcase: viva-amici — AMICI/CVODES compiled ODE integration as a pluggable engine
description: viva-amici bridges AMICI (the Advanced Multi-language Interface to CVODES/IDAS) into process-bigraph as a process that translates an Antimony model to C++, compiles it, and integrates it with the CVODES stiff solver. This showcase proves the bridge on the simplest possible model — exponential decay — the smoke test that compilation, integration, and emission all work; Lotka-Volterra and a MAPK cascade are available as additional registered composites.
question: Does viva-amici expose the AMICI simulator (CVODES, with per-model C++ compilation) as a process-bigraph process that compiles an ODE model, integrates it, and emits a correct time-series?
hypothesis: Wrapping AMICI as a process-bigraph process and running a single-species first-order decay (dA/dt = -kA) should compile the model to native code and integrate it to the analytic solution A(t) = A0*exp(-kt) within solver tolerance, confirming the AMICI->process-bigraph bridge end to end.

executive.what_is_this: A demonstration that the AMICI ODE simulator can be driven as a plug-in engine inside process-bigraph. It compiles a one-equation decay model to native code, integrates it, and reports the concentration falling over time — the baseline proof that the compiled-solver bridge works.
executive.verdict: The exponential-decay composite compiles and runs AMICI end to end: the state falls monotonically to A(5) = 3.6788, matching the analytic 10*exp(-0.2*5) to within 2e-7 — the acceptance band met in a clean-venv run of the pinned engine.
executive.verdict_detail: Study exponential-decay: AMICI generated and compiled C++ for the model, and CVODES integrated it to A(5) = 3.678794 versus analytic 3.678794 (relative error 2.0e-7), strictly monotone decreasing (observed on pbg-amici @ main / AMICI 1.2.0, Apple clang, 2026-11-27).

scientific_argument.main_claim: AMICI can be exposed as a reusable process-bigraph process that compiles an ODE model to native code, integrates it with CVODES, and emits a correct time-series.
evidence_for: The integrated trajectory matches the closed-form exponential solution to ~7 digits, so the compiled model and the stiff solver are genuinely correct.
AMICI emitted C++ sources and a compiled .so on first run, confirming the bridge drives the real compile-then-integrate pipeline, not a stub.
evidence_against: This is a one-state smoke-test model; it proves the bridge, not AMICI's full capability surface (sensitivities, events, larger stiff systems).
caveats: The first run requires a working C/C++ toolchain for AMICI's per-model compilation; on a host without one the engine would be install-deferred.

findings.name: analytic-match
findings.statement: AMICI compiled the decay model to native C++ and CVODES integrated it to A(5) = 3.678794 against the analytic 3.678794 (relative error 2.0e-7), strictly monotone decreasing from A0 = 10.
findings.provenance: Observed in an isolated-venv run of the exponential_decay composite on pbg-amici @ main (commit 63ce10b) / AMICI 1.2.0 (Apple clang), 2026-11-27 (reproduced by sims/run.py).
